clue.text: Man declines to come round for bed linen

indicators.note: one word coming round another wraps itself about it, so the man sits inside the declining word

parts.note: the sun sets, i.e. declines, at evening
a man is referred to as he

explanation.surface: A man going downhill is told to come round for some bedding, like a houseguest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declines' looks like refusing an invitation, but it is the sun going down; 'to come round' wraps it about the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets are the large cloth pieces laid on a mattress, the main items of bed linen.

clue.text: Happy with Louis etc, if dancing

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about the floor and end up in a new arrangement

parts.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is cheerful in the company of a man called Louis and others, provided there is dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicitous means apt or well chosen, and in older use fortunate or joyful, close to happy as in a happy phrase.

clue.text: Removing coat, cook bird

indicators.note: read as re-moving: the letters are moved about again into a fresh order

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: pluck off the feathers, then cook the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing coat' reads like plucking, but 'Removing' is split as re-moving, and the coat and the cook together supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatoo is a crested parrot of Australasia, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Starts fiddling with switch on judge's black box

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the beginning of fiddling is wanted

parts.note: opening letter
to light a lamp is to switch it on
in England a recorder is a barrister sitting as a part-time judge

explanation.surface: Someone tampers with a switch on the black box belonging to a judge, as if evidence were being doctored.
explanation.walkthrough: A recorder is a part-time judge in the English courts, a sense many readers outside Britain will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Black box is the everyday name for the crash-proof device on an aircraft that logs flight data and cockpit sound.

clue.text: Inventing article to be inserted when searching

indicators.note: something inserted is put inside, so the article goes within the other word

parts.note: forging a document is inventing it falsely
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer making up a piece must slot an article in while hunting for material.
explanation.definitionFit: Foraging means hunting around for food or supplies, so it is a kind of searching.

clue.text: In patient about to be admitted, it's up

definitions.note: a noun here, as in ups and downs

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a patient admitted to hospital is taken inside, so the word for about goes within

parts.note: a doctor's patient is a case
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A hospital reports that, with a patient about to be admitted, its numbers have gone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to be admitted' reads as imminent arrival; split it, and 'about' is the short word admitted into the patient.
explanation.definitionFit: An up, as in a rise in figures, is a gain or growth in amount, the noun increase.

clue.text: Expensive letter opener?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the salutation that begins a letter

explanation.walkthrough: A letter opener looks like a paper knife, which could well be pricey; here it is the first word of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means high in price, and it is also the customary greeting written at the head of correspondence.

clue.text: Travelled east after staff

indicators.note: after places the compass point behind the staff in the finished word

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A walker journeyed eastwards following a stick or a group of employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Rode is the past tense of ride, meaning went by horse or vehicle, so travelled.

clue.text: Reprimand after dropping a cake in the rubbish

indicators.note: in places what remains of the cake inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so a letter of the cake is lost

parts.note: taken as written
the letter dropped from the cake

explanation.surface: Someone gets told off after letting a cake fall into the bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reprimand after dropping a cake' reads as one story, but 'after' only joins definition to wordplay. A rocket is British slang for a severe telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to give someone a rocket is to scold them severely, so the noun means a reprimand.

clue.text: Sort to get married and miss embracing dairy worker

indicators.note: one who embraces holds another within the arms, so the miss wraps round the rest

parts.note: a maid is a young unmarried woman, a miss
ilk means sort or kind
abbreviation used in records

explanation.surface: A matchmaker's tale: a fellow sorts himself out to marry and hug a girl who works the dairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkmaid is a woman who milks cows or works in a dairy, a traditional farm worker.

clue.text: Fat father ruined tin of theatrical make-up

parts.note: grease is animal fat

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are broken and rebuilt in a different order

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
taken as written

explanation.surface: A greasy dad has spoilt a tin of stage cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasepaint is the oily coloured cosmetic actors traditionally wear on stage, so it is theatrical make-up.

clue.text: Attractive French lady admitted striking

indicators.note: one admitted is let inside, so the lady sits within the other word

parts.note: pulling as in pulling power, drawing others in
Mme is the abbreviation of Madame

explanation.surface: A glamorous Frenchwoman has been let in and is very eye-catching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like a description of the lady, but here it means hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Pummelling means hitting repeatedly with the fists, a sustained form of striking.

clue.text: Pioneer carelessly lost coin

indicators.note: doing something carelessly throws it into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A frontiersman has been careless and dropped a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist settles a new territory, so is an early settler or pioneer of that land.

clue.text: Big waves miss aunt when swimming

indicators.note: letters swimming drift about freely and settle in another order

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Huge breakers narrowly avoid an aunt taking a dip in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are enormous sea surges set off by earthquakes, the biggest kind of ocean wave.

clue.text: There's no way distilled spirit can be a medicine!

parts.note: taken as written
ST, street, is a way
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: An indignant claim that alcohol cannot possibly count as medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's no way' reads as an idiom of disbelief; split it, and 'way' is a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy or patent medicine of doubtful worth.

clue.text: Which makes a royal person late?

definitions.text: Which makes a royal person late?

parts.words: Which makes a royal person late?
parts.note: surface reading: something that makes a royal running behind schedule
setter's reading: late as in the late king, deceased, so the act of killing a monarch

explanation.walkthrough: Late suggests unpunctual, but it means dead, as in 'the late king'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the killing of a monarch, which turns a living sovereign into the late one.

clue.text: Fragrant ring, the same before turning sour

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter

indicators.note: milk turning goes off and changes, so these letters change their order

parts.note: do is short for ditto, the same
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling ring stays unchanged until it goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning sour' suggests milk going off; 'turning' rearranges the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Odorous means having a distinct smell, and it is often used of a sweet scent, so fragrant.

clue.text: Cafe, as in dull colour, soon takes very little money

indicators.note: in puts the short word within the colour

parts.note: grey is a dull colour
taken as written

indicators.note: a word that takes something holds it inside itself

parts.note: taken as written
p, a penny, is the smallest British coin

explanation.surface: A drab café, painted in dull grey, will soon be taking hardly any cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A penny, P, is very little money in Britain. A greasy spoon is a cheap British café serving fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasy spoon is the informal name for a small cheap eatery serving fried breakfasts, a type of café.

clue.text: When upset, go to God

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
your go in a game is your turn

explanation.surface: An instruction: when you are distressed, turn to God for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to God' reads as one phrase; 'go' is the turn in a game and 'to' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn was the Roman deity of agriculture and time, so he is a god.

clue.text: District standing a long time

indicators.note: standing upright in a down entry means the words are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood that has existed for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or zone of a town or country, so a district.

clue.text: Had zealot hidden a timber dresser?

indicators.note: hidden says the letters lie concealed inside the words just before it

parts.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Asks whether a fanatic had concealed a carpenter's tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dresser' suggests furniture; here it is a tool that dresses, or smooths, wood.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is an axe-like tool with a crosswise blade used for shaping and smoothing rough wood.

clue.text: Laugh at clear clue I made a mess of

parts.note: to rid a place is to clear it

indicators.note: a thing made a mess of is thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter admits botching a clue that should have been plain, and invites mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: To ridicule someone is to mock or make fun of them, which is to laugh at them.

clue.text: An embellishment acceptable in an open court

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: in places the letter for acceptable inside the word for embellishment

parts.note: trim is decoration added to clothing
U, upper-class, means socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A decorative feature is approved for an open courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class, hence socially acceptable, is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is the open central courtyard of a Roman house, or a skylit hall in a modern building.

clue.text: Time to finish making improvements …

parts.note: a.m., morning time
an ending is a finish

explanation.surface: Time to stop revising and wrap things up, the setter says, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Amending means altering a text or law for the better, so it is making improvements.

clue.text: … for nothing great is pointless

indicators.note: pointless here means lacking a point of the compass, so one such letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: making improvements for no reward makes greatness meaningless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' seems to mean futile, but it means minus a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means free of charge, supplied without payment, which is getting something for nothing.
